title: Police CCTV cameras on regional poles recommended
subtitle: Ira Needles resurfacing sent to Council, speed camera funds, facilities plan, asset management gap, expropriations.
overview: The committee recommended that the Region sign an agreement letting Waterloo Regional Police install CCTV cameras on Regional poles and infrastructure {{vote:m7}}. Debate focused on privacy and the role of artificial intelligence against crime-fighting benefits. Staff said no cameras would go into a municipality until it agrees.

On Ira Needles Boulevard, the proposed $4.5 million resurfacing between Yellow Birch Drive and West Hill Drive was not decided at committee. Councillors asked about reserve impacts and which projects would be pushed back, so the report was referred to the May Council meeting {{vote:m6}}, where staff are to add more information.

The committee also recommended a road safety reserve allocation model for former speed camera revenue and provincial funding {{vote:m8}}, and a $350,000 Corporate Facilities Strategic Plan {{vote:m9}}. It recommended expropriation steps for Victoria Street improvements in Kitchener and a surplus land sale in Cambridge. It received the annual asset management update for information, which reported an infrastructure funding gap of $87.6 million per year. It also heard from a transit delegation about on-demand first and last mile service.

decisions.item: Police CCTV cameras on Regional infrastructure
decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing an agreement with the Waterloo Regional Police Service Board to install CCTV cameras on Regional lands and infrastructure {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended referring the report on the proposed $4.5 million resurfacing to the May Council meeting rather than approving it now {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended a Road Safety Reserve allocation model, a provincial Road Safety Initiatives Fund Round 2 application for the Region and area municipalities, and authority to sign the transfer payment agreement {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended developing the plan, including workplace planning, with $350,000 from the General Tax Supported Capital Reserve and about 12 months to complete {{vote:m9}}.
The committee recommended expropriating partial lands and temporary and permanent easements for Victoria Street South improvements between Lawrence Avenue and Fischer Hallman Road in Kitchener.

decisions.item: Victoria Street North expropriation, first report
decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing the Regional Solicitor to begin expropriation steps for a partial taking at 247 Duke Street West for road improvements {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended declaring former George Street North right-of-way lands in Cambridge surplus and selling them to adjacent owners for $26,094 plus taxes and costs.

debate: On Ira Needles, some councillors said they lacked the full picture of which projects would be delayed to fund the $4.5 million. They raised reserve balances and a rural road waiting for resurfacing. Staff said the Q2 financial review would show which projects slip and that waiting means rising patching costs.

Some councillors suggested cheaper methods, such as recycling asphalt in place. Staff said the lowest bid would be pursued, and that tender results could come back to Council. Others said deferral risked missing the construction season. A request for the business case and capital plan excerpt was added to the report going to Council.

On CCTV, opponents raised privacy and the use of AI, said the province had rolled back speed cameras, and preferred more police presence on the ground. Supporters cited theft and crime investigations, consultation with the privacy commissioner, 30-day retention and the need for area municipality agreement.
Police said AI is used only for searches with a human reviewing results, and that cameras can be moved. Staff said the Region's cost would be minimal.

On the facilities plan, one councillor questioned the cost and a consultant, and suggested a shorter, cheaper process. Staff said outside expertise was needed and that return-to-office scenarios and the former police site, once remediation is done, could be addressed.
